source_refs.note: Exercise 11.3, Question 2: book page 295 (instruction for Q1-Q5). The book prints no answers for Unit 11.

blocks.prompt: 2 Find the velocity, acceleration, speed, and direction of motion of the particle with position vector \(\mathbf{r}(t) = e^{t}\hat{i} + e^{-t}\hat{j}\) at \(t = 0\). Interpret the results by describing the particle's motion at that instant, including how fast and in what direction it is moving, whether it is speeding up or slowing down, and how its path is curving.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh Question 1 jaisa hi sawal hai, bas components ab exponential hain.
Diya kya hai? \(\mathbf{r}(t) = e^{t}\hat{i} + e^{-t}\hat{j}\) aur \(t = 0\).
Find kya karna hai? Velocity, acceleration, speed, direction aur harkat ka bayan.
Rule: \(e^{t}\) ka derivative wohi rehta hai, lekin \(e^{-t}\) par chain rule lagta hai jo ek minus deta hai.
Plan: differentiate, \(t = 0\) rakho (\(e^{0} = 1\)), phir \(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{a}\) se tashreeh.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = e^{t}\hat{i} + e^{-t}\hat{j}\), \(t = 0\).
Maloom karna: velocity, acceleration, speed, direction of motion aur tashreeh.
Tareeqa: har component ko ek dafa differentiate kar ke \(\mathbf{v}(t)\), dobara kar ke \(\mathbf{a}(t)\), phir \(t = 0\) rakhna. Speed \(= |\mathbf{v}|\) aur direction \(= \frac{\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{v}|}\). Tashreeh (interpretation) ke liye: \(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{a}\) ka sign batata hai ke particle tez ho raha hai ya dheema, aur \(\mathbf{a}\) ka jo hissa \(\mathbf{v}\) ke aar paar hai woh batata hai ke path kis taraf mur raha hai.

Velocity
\[\mathbf{v}(t) = e^{t}\hat{i} - e^{-t}\hat{j}\]
\[\mathbf{v}(0) = e^{0}\hat{i} - e^{0}\hat{j} = \hat{i} - \hat{j}\]
Kyun: \(e^{t}\) ka derivative \(e^{t}\) hi hai. \(e^{-t}\) mein power \(-t\) hai, to chain rule se power ka derivative \(-1\) saath multiply hota hai: \(\frac{d}{dt}e^{-t} = -e^{-t}\). Aur \(e^{0} = 1\).
Dhyan dein: yahi minus bhool jana sab se aam ghalti hai; us se \(\mathbf{v}(0) = \hat{i} + \hat{j}\) aa jata hai jo ghalat hai.

Acceleration
\[\mathbf{a}(t) = e^{t}\hat{i} + e^{-t}\hat{j}\]
\[\mathbf{a}(0) = \hat{i} + \hat{j}\]
Kyun: \(-e^{-t}\) ka derivative \(-(-e^{-t}) = +e^{-t}\); do minus mil kar plus ban gaye.

Speed
\[|\mathbf{v}(t)| = \sqrt{e^{2t} + e^{-2t}}\]
\[|\mathbf{v}(0)| = \sqrt{1 + 1} = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.41\]
Kyun: \((e^{t})^{2} = e^{2t}\) aur \((-e^{-t})^{2} = e^{-2t}\); square karne se minus khatam ho jata hai.

Direction of motion
\[\hat{\mathbf{v}}(0) = \dfrac{\hat{i} - \hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{i} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{j}\]
Kyun: velocity ko speed se divide kiya. Yeh simt positive \(x\)-axis se \(45^{\circ}\) neeche hai, kyunke \(x\) aur \(y\) hisse barabar hain aur \(y\) wala negative hai.

Tashreeh (interpretation)
Position: \(\mathbf{r}(0) = \hat{i} + \hat{j}\), yani point \((1, 1)\). Particle \(\sqrt{2} \approx 1.41\) units per second se daayen aur neeche ki taraf ja raha hai.
\[\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{a} = (1)(1) + (-1)(1) = 0\]
To is lamhe speed nahin badal rahi. Aur \(e^{2t} + e^{-2t} \ge 2\) har \(t\) ke liye (do positive numbers jin ka product 1 ho, un ka jama kam az kam 2 hota hai), is liye \(\sqrt{2}\) sab se kam speed hai: \(t = 0\) se pehle particle dheema ho raha tha aur baad mein tez hoga.
Path: \(xy = e^{t}e^{-t} = 1\), yani hyperbola. Acceleration \(\hat{i} + \hat{j}\) velocity ke perpendicular hai aur upar daayen, origin se door, ishara karta hai. Is liye path origin se door ki taraf mur raha hai, bilkul jaise hyperbola \(xy = 1\) point \((1, 1)\) par murta hai.
Kyun: \(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{a}\) ka sign speed ka faisla karta hai, aur \(\mathbf{a}\) ka aar paar wala hissa morne ka.

Khulasa
Ek nazar mein: particle point \((1, 1)\) par hai, daayen neeche \(45^{\circ}\) ki simt mein \(\sqrt{2}\) units per second se ja raha hai, us lamhe speed sab se kam hai, aur path origin se door mur raha hai. Ghaur kijiye ke yahan bhi Question 1 ki tarah \(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{a} = 0\) aaya, lekin sirf ek lamhe ke liye; is liye speed us lamhe ruki hui (na barhti na ghatti) hai, hamesha ke liye constant nahin. Constant speed tab hoti hai jab \(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{a} = 0\) har \(t\) ke liye ho, jaise Question 3 mein.

Tasdeeq
\((1, 1)\) par hyperbola \(y = \frac{1}{x}\) ka slope \(-\frac{1}{x^{2}} = -1\) hai, aur \(\mathbf{v} = \hat{i} - \hat{j}\) ki simt ka slope bhi \(-1\) hai. Yani velocity waqai path ka tangent hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(\mathbf{v}(0) = \hat{i} - \hat{j}\), \(\mathbf{a}(0) = \hat{i} + \hat{j}\), speed \(= \sqrt{2} \approx 1.41\), direction \(\hat{\mathbf{v}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{i} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{j}\) (positive \(x\)-axis se \(45^{\circ}\) neeche). Is lamhe speed nahin badal rahi (sab se kam speed), aur path (hyperbola \(xy = 1\)) origin se door mur raha hai.

blocks.text: Kitab mein Exercise 11.3 ke jawab chhape hue nahin hain (Unit 11 ki kisi exercise ke jawab kitab mein nahin hain). Is page ka har jawab hamara apna hai: qadam ba qadam hal kiya gaya, computer algebra system (sympy) se alag se check kiya gaya, aur ek solution book se bhi milaya gaya. \(t = \frac{\pi}{2}\) jaise angles radians mein hain, is liye calculator RAD mode mein rakhein. Apna hal yahan wale hal se mila kar dekhiye.
